title: Model timeline reconciliation for deferred streaming billing
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: Several customers and internal dashboards show transient per-model spikes and apparent token double-counting when deferred streaming events are ingested during backfills. Root cause analysis indicates inconsistent timestamp assignment and missing ingest_origin metadata for streaming-derived token events. When late events are replayed, the current rollup jobs sometimes create overlapping buckets and the console's per-model heatmaps surface amplified artifacts.
problem_statement: Deferred streaming events (prefix tokens, KV cache continuations) are occasionally written with ingestion_time or synthetic timestamps that do not correspond to the original event timeline. Aggregations use a mix of event_time and ingestion_time depending on pipeline stage, which leads to: 1) sudden spikes in per-model daily totals after backfills, 2) apparent token duplication across models when requests are retried, and 3) misleading cost attribution in Console charts. We need a deterministic reconciliation approach so the console reflects canonical usage and backfills are safe and idempotent.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a canonical_event_time field at the earliest ingress (agent/proxy/runtime). 2) Preserve ingest_origin and replay_id metadata for all streaming and backfilled events. 3) Implement a timeline-reconciliation job (reconciler) that: a) groups events by canonical_event_time rounded to an adjustable coverage window, b) fingerprint sequences (request_id + token_range + replay_id) to dedupe duplicates, c) recomputes per-model / per-route aggregates into a reconciled-timeseries store. 4) Add a thin migration that applies reconciler fixes to recent 30 days and a long-running repair job for older history. 5) Surface reconciled vs raw series in the Console with an explanation tooltip and provenance link.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model daily totals for a 30-day test window must match the canonical billing ledger within 0.5%
Backfill runs are idempotent and do not increase already-reconciled totals
Console provides a toggle to view 'reconciled' vs 'raw' time series and shows a provenance link for reconciled windows
Repair job exposes metrics: processed_events, deduped_events, adjusted_tokens, run_duration
Unit, integration, and end-to-end tests covering duplicate detection and coverage-window boundary conditions are present and passing
implementation_steps: Schema: add canonical_event_time, ingest_origin, replay_id to streaming event envelope (runtime+ingest) and update producers
Ingest changes: ensure gateways runtime and only-once semantics for replay_id propagation
Reconciler prototype: lambda to group and fingerprint events for a single 24h shard
Rollup changes: consumer reads reconciled-timeseries store when available and falls back to raw-aggregates
Console: UI changes to expose reconciled toggle and provenance panel (copy + link to repair job run details)
Backfill safety: design repair job throttling and checkpointing to avoid high I/O and CPU spikes
Testing: synthetic workload that simulates network replays, out-of-order arrival, and partial duplicates
Deploy: staged rollout (canary in staging -> canary in prod region -> global) and monitor key metrics
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Reconciler may lag and produce visible divergence during initial deployment. Mitigation: expose both raw and reconciled series and default to raw for <48h windows until reconciler catches up.

Risk: Fingerprinting false-positives could drop legitimate retries. Mitigation: conservative fingerprint (include request_id, token_range, replay_id, model_version) and add a TTL for fingerprints before dedupe applies.
Risk: High I/O while repairing large historical windows. Mitigation: shard repair by time and model, rate-limit background repair, and schedule heavy jobs during low-traffic windows
observability_and_metrics: dashboard: reconciler-run-{shard} showing processed_events, deduped_count, tokens_adjusted, error_rate
SLOs: reconciler 95th percentile run_duration < 45m for 24h shard
Console telemetry: user_toggle_usage for reconciled vs raw for UX analysis

2026-03-03 Aisha Kaur: Drafted reconciler proto and ran tests against synthetic dataset (10M events). Initial dedupe reduced apparent tokens by ~12% in a noisy bucket.
2026-03-05 Design review: Console UX will show 'reconciled' as opt-in default for Customers on Dedicated; hosted users see a banner explaining reconciliation latency.
2026-03-08 Security review (notes): no new secrets; confirm that replay_id does not contain PII — security confirmed.
2026-03-10 QA: Found edge-case where coverage window boundary split a long-running request across two buckets causing a small mismatch — adding unit test to cover window alignment.
